name: cars_fleet_a
prompt:
Two images are attached. The first is a layout: 9 car outlines seen from above, in a 3×3 grid on a flat magenta background. Every outline is the car's true length and width on one shared scale, its corners rounded as that body is, and the thick right edge of each one is the car's nose: every car points to the right. The second image shows finished cars in the art style to match. Copy its style only, not its cars or colours.

Make one image with exactly the same 3×3 layout as the first image. Inside each outline, draw the car described for that cell below, as a top-down sprite for a 2D city game. Each is a believable everyday car of a real kind, as seen in an Eastern European city today.

Shape comes first:
- Trace each outline like paint on tracing paper laid over it: same length, same width, same corner rounding, nose at the thick edge. Do not re-centre or resize anything. The car's two long sides lie on the outline's top and bottom edges: never wider than the outline, never narrower, never shorter or longer.
- The only things allowed past the outline are the two side mirrors, one each side just ahead of the windscreen. Keep them small: each no longer than the headlamp and reaching out only a few pixels. The last attempt drew them twice that size.
- Do not draw tyres or wheels at all: the game draws them itself under the body.
- Every car has its roof on. No convertible, no open top, no visible seats or people.
- Each car is mirror-symmetric about its long centre line.
- Inside a car there is no magenta at all.

Lamps — ten lenses on every car, each in its own thin coloured frame, mirror-symmetric:
- At each front (right) corner, one headlamp unit: clear headlamp glass with a chrome reflector filling the blue frame, and its amber indicator lens filling the small amber frame right at the corner, on the side towards the car's flank.
- At each rear (left) corner, one rear lamp cluster laid along the tail edge, three frames side by side from the flank inwards: the dark red frame nearest the flank is the red tail and brake lamp; the amber frame next to it is the rear indicator; the dark grey frame innermost is the reversing lamp.
- The rear cluster is three different colours of glass, not one. Seen from above, going along the tail edge from the corner towards the middle: a red block, then a bright orange-amber block, then a small clear white block. The last attempt drew every rear cluster as one all-red lamp with no orange and no white in it: that is wrong. Every car here has an orange rear indicator and a white reversing lamp in each rear cluster, as European cars do.
- Put each lens inside its own frame.
- Every car has all ten lenses: two headlamps, two front indicators, two red tail lamps, two rear indicators, two reversing lamps.
- Every lamp is switched off: dark unlit glass with one small pale glint, no glow, no light cast on the body or the ground.
- The frames themselves are guides only; do not draw their lines.

Rules for every car:
- Look straight down (orthographic). No perspective, no tilt, no side panels, no ground, no shadow.
- Style: match the style image. Pixel art with crisp hard-edged pixels and no blur. A dark near-black outline about 2 pixels thick. Flat colour with one highlight and one shadow tone. Soft light from the top-left. Glass is dark slate blue with one pale glint.
- Bonnet, roof and boot read as separate panels, divided by the windscreen and the rear window.
- No text, logos, brand badges, licence plates, numbers, people or watermark anywhere.
- Outside the cars, keep the background flat pure magenta #FF00FF. No grid lines or frames.

Cars, left to right, top to bottom, body length × width (the footprint includes the mirrors):
1. 3.60 × 1.60 m (2.2× longer than wide), rounded corners, its flanks straight and full width from nose to tail; the last attempt drew it about 9% too wide and off-centre in its cell — five-door city car, lime green, a short rounded bonnet, tall roof with one long glass area, a short hatchback tail, slim headlamps swept back into the front wings
2. 4.05 × 1.74 m (2.3× longer than wide), rounded corners — five-door supermini hatchback, bright red, a short sloping bonnet, a rounded roof, a steep hatchback tail with a small spoiler at the top of the rear window
3. 4.13 × 1.62 m (2.5× longer than wide), nearly square corners, long and slim, narrower than a modern car — 1980s Eastern European four-door saloon, faded beige, completely boxy with flat panels and sharp square corners, a long flat bonnet, an upright three-box roof, a separate flat boot, thin chrome bumpers at both ends, square headlamps
4. 4.28 × 1.79 m (2.4× longer than wide), rounded corners — five-door family hatchback, dark graphite grey, a level bonnet with a crease down each side, a long flat roof, a near-vertical hatchback tail, wide rear pillars
5. 4.35 × 1.73 m (2.5× longer than wide), gently rounded corners — plain budget four-door saloon, white, a simple rounded bonnet, a tall roof, a short separate boot lid, black unpainted bumpers and mirrors
6. 4.50 × 1.82 m (2.5× longer than wide), tight corners, its sides exactly on the outline's edges; the last attempt drew it about 11% too wide — tall boxy leisure van with seats, sage green, a short sloping bonnet, a long flat high roof, sliding side doors with their rails showing, a big square tailgate, black bumpers
7. 4.60 × 1.86 m (2.5× longer than wide), rounded corners, its sides exactly on the outline's edges, the black wheel-arch trim inside the outline too; the last attempt drew it about 10% too wide — compact SUV crossover, pearl white with a black roof, a tall squared bonnet, black plastic wheel-arch trim at all four corners, black roof rails, a near-vertical tailgate
8. 4.69 × 1.83 m (2.6× longer than wide), gently rounded corners — family estate car, steel blue, a level bonnet, a long roof running all the way to a squared-off tail with a tall rear window, two thin silver roof rails along the roof edges
9. 4.88 × 1.84 m (2.7× longer than wide), gently rounded corners — mid-size four-door saloon, gloss black, a long low bonnet, a sleek roof sloping into a short boot, a thin chrome strip round the side windows
